A TypeScript project keeps application code in `app.tsx` and development commands in `package.json`.

## Generated files

```text
my-app/
├── app.tsx
├── quickgui.config.ts
├── tsconfig.json
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

Keep reusable components in ordinary TypeScript modules. Build output lives in `.quickgui`; packaged apps live in `dist`.

## Application entry

Import `app` and `Window` from `@quickgui/native`. Import components and `createRenderer` from `@quickgui/solid`. Await `app.whenReady()` before opening windows. Each window has its own renderer, disposed when the window closes.

## Configuration

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@quickgui/cli";

export default defineConfig({
  language: "typescript",
  name: "My App",
  identifier: "com.example.my-app",
  entry: "app.tsx",
  icon: "assets/icon.png",
  fonts: ["assets/MyFont.ttf"],
  resources: ["assets"],
});
```

See [App Icon](/docs/typescript/app-icon) and [Bundled Resources](/docs/typescript/bundled-resources). TOML supports the same keys. In `tsconfig.json`, set `jsx` to `"preserve"` and `jsxImportSource` to `"@quickgui/solid"`.

## Packages

Applications depend on `@quickgui/native`, `@quickgui/solid`, and `solid-js`. `@quickgui/cli` is a development dependency. Terminal and updater are optional packages — see [Auto Updater](/docs/typescript/updater) and [Authoring Extensions](/docs/typescript/extensions).

## Local development

```sh
quickgui check
quickgui test
quickgui fmt
quickgui dev
quickgui build
```

`check` typechecks the project. `test` runs tests with the same compiler as builds.
